steps.title: Bright and pure
steps.body: Riesling gives whites with lime, lemon, green apple, peach, apricot and white flowers, with a mineral, sometimes smoky edge. Acidity is very high. It's almost never oaked or put through malolactic, so its fruit is pure and transparent. It ranges from bone dry to intensely sweet, and from light to full-bodied.

steps.title: German origins
steps.body: Riesling comes from the Rhine valley in Germany, first recorded in 1435 near Rüsselsheim. DNA shows one parent is Gouais Blanc; the other was a Traminer crossed with a wild vine. It buds late and ripens late, so it needs a long season. Its hard wood resists winter cold well, ideal for northern vineyards.

steps.prompt: Why is Riesling's fruit so pure and transparent?
options: It's rarely oaked or put through malolactic
steps.explanation: Without oak or malolactic, nothing masks its fruit or place.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon, sometimes green-tinged colour, intense lime, apple and flower aromas, and very high acidity. Sweet versions balance sugar with that acidity. Aged Riesling shows honey, toast and a petrol note. High acidity with floral, citrus fruit and no oak is the signature.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling gives lime, peach and flowers with very high acidity
It comes from the Rhine, recorded in 1435
It's rarely oaked, so it shows fruit and place clearly
